spans.s:
Yudhāṃ-śrauṣṭi augra-sainya (‘descendant of ugrasena’) is the name, in the aitareya brāhmaṇa, of a king who was anointed by parvata and nārada.
Foot notes viii. 21, 7. Cf. Weber, Episches im vedischen Ritual, 8. The Paurāṇic form is yuddha-muṣṭi.

Yudhyāmadhi is apparently the name of a king who was defeated by sudās. The mention of him occurring only in the verses added at the end of the hymn celebrating the victory of sudās over the ten kings can claim little authenticity as a notice of sudās.
Foot notes Rv. vii. 18, 24. Cf. Ludwig, Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 173.
